#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Analyze video frames to find chapter timestamps based on visual patterns.
This script will help identify when chapters appear in the video.
"""

import os
import json

# Chapter list we're looking for
chapters = [
    "What we'll do",
    "How we'll get there",
    "Getting a floor plan",
    "Getting started",
    "Basic Navigation",
    "Import your plan into Blender",
    "Basic transform operations",
    "Setting up the plan and units",
    "It all starts with a plane",
    "Scaling the plane to real dimensions",
    "Getting the plan in place",
    "Tracing the outline",
    "Tracing inner walls",
    "Break",
    "Continue tracing inner walls",
    "Remove doubled vertices",
    "Save",
    "Make the floor",
    "Remove unnecessary geometry",
    "Make the floor's faces",
    "Make the background",
    "Extruding the walls in Z",
    "Reviewing face orientation",
    "Adding thickness to walls with Modifiers",
    "Fixing face orientation errors",
    "Note on face orientation",
    "Save As",
    "If you need thick and thin walls",
    "Great job!"
]

# List all frames
frames_dir = "/root/video_frames"
frames = sorted([f for f in os.listdir(frames_dir) if f.endswith('.png')])

print(f"Total frames: {len(frames)}")
print(f"Total chapters to find: {len(chapters)}")
print(f"\nFrames are extracted every 2 seconds")
print(f"Video length: 1382 seconds")
print(f"Expected frame count: ~691")

# Calculate frame number to timestamp
def frame_to_timestamp(frame_num):
    """Convert frame number to timestamp in seconds (frames are every 2 seconds)"""
    return (frame_num - 1) * 2

# Print frame numbers for reference
print("\n\nKey frame numbers for manual inspection:")
for i in [1, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450, 500, 550, 600, 650, 691]:
    if i <= len(frames):
        print(f"Frame {i:04d}: {frame_to_timestamp(i)} seconds - {frames[i-1]}")
